questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the claim state that the increase is a step fixed in advance in the lease, by which the rent rises periodically by fixed amounts (graduated rent)?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the claim state that, together with the rent increase, the landlord gave notice of termination?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the increase notice give, as its reason, higher costs for the landlord (for example higher mortgage interest or operating costs) or additional services or works by the landlord (for example a renovation)?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the claim state that the increase applies a clause of the lease linking the rent to an index (such as the Swiss consumer price index)?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord has announced, demanded or charged a higher rent for the dwelling, by a notice, a letter, an invoice or otherwise (whether or not on an official form)?

text:
Good afternoon,

I moved into a 3.5-room flat at Mühleweg 11 in Neuchâtel in January 2022. The landlord is Rebhalde Holdings Ltd and my contact there is Ms Sophie Frei. I pay CHF 2860 a month, which has always felt steep.

On 23 January 2026 I got talking to my neighbour Tom Näf, who has the same layout two floors down, and found out he pays several hundred francs less than I do. That really got to me. I want to understand whether I can ask Rebhalde to lower my rent, and how I would go about it.

Just so there is no confusion: my rent has never gone up. In four years Rebhalde has not sent me any letter or form saying the rent would rise, nobody has asked me for more money, and every bill and standing order is still for exactly CHF 2860. My problem is that I think I have been paying too much from the start, not that they want more.

I'd be grateful for a short reply on whether it is worth pursuing.

Kind regards,
Alice Huber
